arguments.command:
cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'PYEOF'
# CPU policy agent

`driver.py` is the collected JSON entry point: it reads one request from stdin,
validates the whole-request envelope and every job, replays each valid job and
writes one response to stdout.

Module layout:

* `syntax.py` — the public policy language: lexer, recursive-descent parser and
  the declared per-string bounds.  It never evaluates predicates.
* `compiler/compiler.py` — the language algebra.  Parsed rules become hash-consed
  language expressions; the Brzozowski derivative closure enumerates the
  residuals into a deterministic complete automaton, Moore refinement
  minimises it and `canonical()` exports the live-state table (dead residual
  removed, START always retained, breadth-first numbering with columns in
  increasing service-label order, DENY for dead transitions).
* `ebpf/create_dfa.py` — the state exporter: parse + compile + canonical
  numbering into the immutable image `{accept, rows}` plus its cell count.
* `ebpf/helper.py` — the CPU map backend and replay engine.  `Agent` installs
  images atomically, pins contexts to epochs, accounts references exactly
  (live context copies, retained packets, current files) and replays every
  operation all-or-nothing.
* `driver.py` — strict JSON ingress (duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, 4300
  digit integers, 64 container levels, UTF-8/BOM rules), job validation,
  whole-request budget accounting and response encoding.

Kernel attachment, service deployment and packet capture are outside this
project.  The offline packages under `/opt/emicro-deps` are already supplied;
do not install dependencies.  Run `python3 /workspace/launch.py < request.json`
and `python3 /workspace/public_check.py` as a nonroot user.
PYEOF
cd /workspace && rm -rf project/__pycache__ project/*/__pycache__ && for t in t_lifecycle t_units t_transport t_files t_json t_edges t_policy; do printf "%-14s " $t; python3 tests/$t.py 2>&1 | tail -1; done; timeout 600 python3 tests/t_diff.py 2>&1|tail -1; timeout 900 python3 tests/t_scale.py 2>&1|tail -4; python3 public_check.py
